content: The medication may be less effective in young children. During pregnancy, it should only be used if absolutely necessary. It is not known whether this drug passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Interactions with other drugs may alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not list all possible drug interactions. Keep a detailed list of all products you use, including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Inform your doctor if you have received a nasal flu vaccine in the past two weeks, as zanamivir may interfere with the vaccine's effectiveness if administered too closely together. Overdose: If someone overdoses and experiences severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. In the U.S., you can call 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current condition and is not a substitute for the flu vaccine. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose (within two hours), skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Storage: Store the medication at room temperature in a dry place. Do not puncture the foil blister until you are ready to use it. Avoid storing it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard the product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This document provides a summary and does not include all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Uses: Zanamivir is used to treat flu symptoms caused by the influenza virus if symptoms have been present for two days or less. It may also be used to prevent the flu if you have been exposed to someone with the flu or during a community outbreak. This medication works by inhibiting the growth of the flu virus. How to Use: Read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist before starting zanamivir and each time you get a refill. Follow all usage instructions carefully. For flu treatment, inhale the medication through your mouth as directed by your doctor, usually two inhalations (one blister per inhalation) twice daily, about 12 hours apart, for five days. For flu prevention, inhale two inhalations once daily as directed. Load the medication disk into the inhaler, puncture one blister, and keep the inhaler level to prevent spillage. Exhale fully, place the mouthpiece in your mouth, and inhale deeply to draw the medication into your lungs. Hold your breath for a few seconds. If a second inhalation is needed, advance to the next blister and repeat the process. Start zanamivir as soon as possible for best results. Continue using the medication for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve. If you have breathing problems such as asthma or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and are scheduled to use inhaled bronchodilators (e.g., albuterol) at the same time as zanamivir, use the bronchodilator first. Side Effects: Dizziness may occur. As this medication is an inhaled powder, you may experience increased coughing after use. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks. However, zanamivir can cause breathing problems, which in rare cases may be fatal. If you experience wheezing or shortness of breath, stop using the medication and seek medical help immediately. Zanamivir is not recommended for individuals with lung or breathing problems. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor. The flu itself or zanamivir may rarely cause serious mental or mood changes, which may be more likely in children. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Precautions: Before using zanamivir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients (e.g., lactose, milk proteins) that can cause allergic reactions or other issues. This drug may cause dizziness, and alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, using machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. During pregnancy, use this medication only when clearly needed. It is unknown if this drug passes into breast milk. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
